classification.difficultyReason: Translate the amount melted into remaining mass, solve for the corresponding time, then evaluate and interpret the signed derivative as a rate of mass loss.

content.prompt: A block of ice of mass 8 kg melts according to the formula $$M=8-\frac{t^2}{32},$$ where $M$ is the mass remaining, in kilograms, after $t$ minutes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the time taken for all the ice to melt.

answer.worked: When all the ice has melted, $M=0$. $$\begin{align*}8-\frac{t^2}{32}&=0\\t^2&=256\\t&=16\ \mathrm{min}\qquad(t\ge 0).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting after 4 minutes.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting when 2 kg of ice has melted.

answer.short:
The mass decreases at $0.5\ \mathrm{kg/min}$, so $M'(8)=-0.5\ \mathrm{kg/min}$.

Use the time when 6 kg of ice remains.
answer.worked: When 2 kg has melted, $8-2=6$ kg remains. $$\begin{align*}8-\frac{t^2}{32}&=6\\t^2&=64\\t&=8\ \mathrm{min}\qquad(t\ge 0).\end{align*}$$ Using $M'(t)=-\frac{t}{16}$, $$M'(8)=-\frac{8}{16}=-0.5\ \mathrm{kg/min}.$$ The ice loses mass at $0.5\ \mathrm{kg/min}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Is the melting rate faster initially, or just before it is gone completely?

answer.short: Just before all the ice is gone.
answer.worked: The rate of mass loss is $-M'(t)=\frac{t}{16}$. It starts at $0\ \mathrm{kg/min}$ and increases to nearly $1\ \mathrm{kg/min}$ just before $t=16$, so the ice melts faster just before it is gone.
